events.enhanced_description: Around 710 BC, Assyrian king Sargon II successfully conquered the Neo-Hittite state of Carchemish, a strategic victory that expanded Assyrian influence in the region. This conquest was part of Sargon's broader military campaigns that established Assyria as a dominant power in the ancient Near East.
events.name: Sargon conquers the Neo-Hittite state of Carchemish

events.enhanced_description: Around 710 BC, Sargon II founded Dur-Sharrukin, a new capital for the Assyrian Empire, which was designed to showcase the power and wealth of his reign. The city was notable for its impressive architecture and served as a political and administrative center.
events.name: Sargon II founds a new capital for Assyria at Dur-Sharrukin

events.enhanced_description: Pythagoras of Laconia's victory in the stadion race at the 16th Olympic Games is a notable event in ancient Greek athletic history. This race was a highlight of the Olympic Games, emphasizing the importance of athletic competition in Greek culture.
events.name: Pythagoras of Laconia wins the stadion race at the 16th Olympic Games

events.enhanced_description: The end of the Interregnum around 710 BC marked the beginning of Numa Pompilius's reign as the second king of Rome. Numa is credited with establishing many of Rome's religious and cultural institutions, shaping the city's early development.
events.name: End of the Interregnum and start of Numa Pompilius's reign

events.enhanced_description: Around 710 BC, the Medes, an ancient Iranian people, achieved unification under the leadership of Deioces, marking the beginning of the Median Empire. This unification set the stage for the Medes to become a significant power in the region, eventually leading to their role in the downfall of the Assyrian Empire.
events.name: Unification of the Medes

events.enhanced_description: Around 710 BCE, the Medes, an ancient Iranian people, successfully united under a single leadership, marking a significant moment in the formation of the Median Empire. This unification laid the foundation for the Medes to become a dominant power in the region, influencing the future of Persia and its neighbors.
events.name: The Medes are united

events.enhanced_description: Atheradas of Laconia triumphed in the stadion race, a prestigious event at the 20th Olympic Games held in Olympia, Greece. This victory not only highlighted his athletic prowess but also contributed to the competitive spirit of the ancient Olympic tradition, which celebrated physical excellence and honor.
events.name: Atheradas of Laconia wins the stadion race at the 20th Olympic Games

events.enhanced_description: The composition of the Upanishads, a collection of philosophical texts central to Hindu thought, represents a significant development in Indian spirituality and philosophy. These texts explore profound concepts such as the nature of reality and the self, influencing generations of thinkers.
events.name: The Upanishads are written

events.enhanced_description: The Assyrian royal court was relocated to Dur-Sharrukin, a city built by Sargon II as a new capital. This move was part of Sargon II's efforts to consolidate power and establish a more secure and strategically advantageous seat of government.
events.name: The Assyrian royal court is moved to Dur-Sharrukin

events.enhanced_description: Sargon II, the king of Assyria, died, marking the end of his reign which was characterized by military conquests and the establishment of Dur-Sharrukin as the capital. His death led to a succession crisis and significant changes in Assyrian politics.
events.name: Sargon II, king of Assyria, dies

events.enhanced_description: Following the death of Sargon II, his son Sennacherib ascended to the throne of Assyria. Sennacherib's reign would be marked by military campaigns and the further development of the Assyrian capital at Nineveh.
events.name: Sennacherib succeeds his father Sargon II

events.enhanced_description: Sennacherib moved the capital of Assyria from Dur-Sharrukin to Nineveh, which would become one of the largest and most important cities in the ancient world. This strategic relocation was part of his efforts to strengthen the empire and enhance its administrative capabilities.
events.name: Sennacherib moves the capital of Assyria to Nineveh

events.enhanced_description: Menos of Megara triumphed in the stadion race at the 19th Olympic Games, a prestigious event in ancient Greece that celebrated athletic prowess and religious devotion. This victory contributed to the legacy of the Olympic Games as a central aspect of Greek culture.
events.name: Menos of Megara wins the stadion race at the 19th Olympic Games

events.enhanced_description: The settlement of Scythians in Cimmerian territories marked a significant demographic shift in the region, leading to cultural and social changes as they replaced previous inhabitants. This migration played a key role in the historical development of the area.
events.name: The Scythians start settling in Cimmerian areas

events.enhanced_description: The decline of the Villanovan culture in northern Italy paved the way for the rise of the Etruscan civilization, which would become a dominant force in the region. This transition marked a significant cultural evolution in ancient Italy.
events.name: End of the Villanovan culture in northern Italy and rise of the Etruscan civilization

events.enhanced_description: The construction of the Temple of Yeha in Ethiopia represents a significant achievement in the architectural and religious landscape of the region. This temple is one of the oldest monumental structures in Ethiopia, reflecting the cultural and religious practices of the ancient civilizations that inhabited the area.
events.name: Construction of the Temple of Yeha in Ethiopia

events.enhanced_description: The Dorians established Poseidonia, a Greek colony, as an offshoot of Sybaris. This settlement became known for its well-preserved ruins and was a significant cultural center in ancient Italy, reflecting the influence of Greek civilization in the region.
events.name: Founding of Poseidonia by the Dorians as a colony of Sybaris

events.enhanced_description: In a bid to consolidate his power, Assyrian king Sennacherib launched a military campaign into the Chaldean region to confront the Babylonian rebel Merodach-Baladan II. This conflict marked a significant moment in the power struggle between Assyria and Babylon, with Merodach-Baladan seeking refuge in Elam to escape Sennacherib's forces.
events.name: Sennacherib's Campaign against Merodach-Baladan II

events.enhanced_description: Bel-ibni, the Assyrian-raised puppet king of Babylon, was deposed after a brief three-year reign. His removal from power was orchestrated by Sennacherib, who installed his son Ashur-nadin-shumi as the new ruler, further asserting Assyrian dominance over Babylon.
events.name: Deposition of Bel-ibni, King of Babylon

events.enhanced_description: The minister of agriculture in ancient China introduced innovative agricultural techniques, including crop rotation and the construction of drainage ditches, to improve farming efficiency. This initiative aimed to enhance food security by storing grain surpluses and providing for the populace during famines.
events.name: Introduction of Crop Rotation in Ancient China

events.enhanced_description: During this period, laws governing animal slaughter in India were relaxed, reflecting changing social and cultural attitudes towards animal husbandry and consumption. This shift may have had significant implications for both agriculture and dietary practices in the region.
events.name: Relaxation of Animal Slaughter Laws in India

events.enhanced_description: As urbanization progressed in the Near East, cities began to construct aqueducts to ensure a reliable water supply for their growing populations. This engineering advancement played a crucial role in the development of these ancient civilizations, facilitating agriculture and urban life.
events.name: Construction of Aqueducts in the Near East

events.enhanced_description: Atheradas of Laconia triumphed in the stadion race during the 20th Olympic Games, a prestigious event in ancient Greece that celebrated athletic prowess and honored the gods. This victory contributed to the cultural significance of the Olympics as a unifying event for the Greek city-states.
events.name: Atheradas Wins the Stadion Race at the 20th Olympic Games

events.enhanced_description: Around 700 BC, the Geometric period of vase painting in Ancient Greece transitioned into the Orientalizing period, marking a significant evolution in artistic styles. This change began in Corinth, where new influences led to more intricate designs and motifs, reflecting broader cultural exchanges.
events.name: End of the Geometric period of vases in Ancient Greece

events.enhanced_description: Around 700 BC, the poet Hesiod composed 'Theogony', a foundational text in Greek literature that outlines the origins and genealogies of the gods. This work not only shaped Greek mythology but also provided insights into the religious beliefs and cultural values of ancient Greece.
events.name: Hesiod writes "Theogony"

events.enhanced_description: After approximately 700 BC, urbanization began to re-emerge on the Indian subcontinent, particularly in the northern regions. This resurgence marked a significant shift in social and economic structures, leading to the development of complex societies and trade networks.
events.name: Cities begin to appear on the Indian subcontinent

events.enhanced_description: The end of the Geometric period of vase painting in Ancient Greece marked a transition to the Orientalizing period, characterized by new artistic influences and styles. This shift began in Corinth and had a profound impact on Greek art and culture.
events.name: Geometric period of vases ends in Ancient Greece

events.enhanced_description: After around 700 BC, urbanization began to re-emerge in Northern India, leading to the establishment of cities that would become centers of trade, culture, and governance. This period marked a significant shift in societal organization on the Indian subcontinent.
events.name: Emergence of cities on the Indian subcontinent

events.enhanced_description: Khallushu's ascension to the throne marked a significant transition in the Elamite Empire, reflecting the ongoing power struggles within the region. His reign would influence the political landscape of Elam and its interactions with neighboring powers.
events.name: Khallushu succeeds Shuttir-Nakhkhunte as king of Elam

events.enhanced_description: The birth of Duke Wen of Jin heralded the arrival of a significant figure in Chinese history, known for his contributions to the Jin state during the Spring and Autumn period. His leadership would later play a crucial role in the political developments of the time.
events.name: Birth of Duke Wen of Jin

events.enhanced_description: The death of King Huan of Zhou marked a significant turning point in the Zhou dynasty, leading to a period of instability and power struggles among the feudal lords. His reign was characterized by efforts to maintain the integrity of the Zhou state amidst growing challenges.
events.name: Death of King Huan of Zhou

events.enhanced_description: The succession of Manasseh following Hezekiah's reign marked a significant shift in the leadership of Judah, with Manasseh's rule noted for its controversial policies and religious reforms. This transition reflected the ongoing struggles within the kingdom and its relations with surrounding powers.
events.name: Hezekiah succeeded by Manasseh as king of Judah

events.enhanced_description: King Zhuang of Zhou's ascension marked the beginning of a new era in the Zhou dynasty, as he sought to consolidate power amidst a fragmented political landscape. His reign would be characterized by efforts to strengthen the authority of the Zhou kingship.
events.name: King Zhuang of Zhou begins his reign

events.enhanced_description: The Cimmerians' invasion and subsequent ravaging of Phrygia marked a significant moment of upheaval in the region, leading to widespread destruction and the potential migration of other groups, such as the Armenians. This event illustrates the turbulent nature of ancient geopolitical dynamics.
events.name: Cimmerians ravage Phrygia

events.enhanced_description: Pantacles of Athens achieved victory in the stadion race at the 21st Olympic Games, a prestigious event that celebrated athletic prowess and cultural unity in ancient Greece. This victory contributed to the legacy of the Olympic Games as a central aspect of Greek culture and identity.
events.name: Pantacles of Athens wins the stadion race

events.enhanced_description: Karib'il Watar of Saba' is recorded as having given tribute to King Sennacherib of Assyria, reflecting the political relationships and dependencies between smaller kingdoms and larger empires during this period. Such tributes were often necessary for maintaining peace and avoiding military conflict.
events.name: Karib'il Watar of Saba' gives tribute to Sennacherib

events.enhanced_description: Duke Xiang of Qi and Duke Huan of Lu convened at Luo, a significant political meeting that underscored the alliances and rivalries among the feudal states during the Spring and Autumn period of Chinese history. This meeting was pivotal in shaping the political landscape of the time.
events.name: Meeting of Duke Xiang of Qi and Duke Huan of Lu

events.enhanced_description: The death of Duke Huan of Lu marked a significant transition in the political dynamics of the region, as he was a prominent figure in the power struggles of the time. His leadership had been instrumental in the consolidation of power among the various states during the Spring and Autumn period.

image.caption: Portrait illustration of Duke Huan of Lu, reproduced in an edition of 《东周列国志》.
image.credit: 冯梦龙、蔡元放 — 《东周列国志》（绣像本）
image.date_qualification: Image date supplied as 1912-01-01; this is not the date of the depicted death or evidence of a contemporary event image.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Death of Duke Huan of Lu

events.enhanced_description: In a violent power struggle, troops from Qi assassinated Zheng-zi Wei, the 7th ruler of Zheng, along with Gao Qumi, indicating the turbulent political climate of the time. This event led to further instability and the eventual rise of Zheng-zi Ying, who was supported by Ji Zhong.
events.name: Troops of Qi kill Zheng-zi Wei and Gao Qumi

events.enhanced_description: Duke Hei Jian's assassination of King Zhuang of Zhou was a pivotal moment in the history of the Zhou dynasty, leading to a power vacuum and subsequent political intrigue. This act of treachery was reported to the king, resulting in Duke Hei Jian's own death, illustrating the brutal nature of court politics at the time.
events.name: Duke Hei Jian of Zhou kills King Zhuang of Zhou

events.enhanced_description: In a decisive military campaign, Sennacherib, the Assyrian king, destroyed the ancient city of Babylon, which had been a significant cultural and political center. Although the city was devastated, it would later be rebuilt, reflecting the resilience and enduring legacy of Babylonian civilization.
events.name: Destruction of Babylon by Sennacherib

events.enhanced_description: Tirhakah, the last pharaoh of the 25th Dynasty, ascended the throne of Egypt, marking a significant moment in the history of the region as he was a ruler of Nubian descent. His reign was characterized by military campaigns against Assyrian forces and efforts to maintain Egyptian sovereignty during a time of external pressures.
events.name: Tirhakah ascends the throne of Egypt

events.enhanced_description: Karib'il Watar, the ruler of the ancient kingdom of Saba, is recorded as having paid tribute to Sennacherib, the king of Assyria. This act of tribute reflects the political dynamics of the time, where smaller kingdoms often sought to maintain peace and stability through such gestures towards more powerful empires.
events.name: Karib'il Watar pays tribute to Sennacherib

events.enhanced_description: In 666 BCE, King Ashurbanipal of Assyria undertook a significant military campaign to Egypt, aiming to consolidate Assyrian power in the region. This campaign was part of his broader strategy to control the Near East.
events.name: King Ashurbanipal undertook a campaign to Egypt

events.enhanced_description: It is theorized that Psammitichus I ascended the throne of Egypt in 666 BCE, marking the beginning of a significant period in Egyptian history characterized by the resurgence of native rule after foreign domination.
events.name: One theory is that this is the year Psammitichus I ascended the throne

events.enhanced_description: In 665 BCE, Elamite king Urtak launched a surprise attack against Babylonia, but his forces were successfully repelled. This conflict highlights the ongoing tensions between the Elamite and Babylonian empires during this period.
events.name: Elamite king Urtak launches a surprise attack against Babylonia but is successfully driven back

events.enhanced_description: In 664 BCE, the Assyrian army, led by King Ashurbanipal, successfully captured and sacked Thebes, a major city in ancient Egypt. This event marked the end of the Nubian period in Egypt, as Assyria asserted its dominance over the region.
events.name: Assyrian army captures and sacks Thebes, Egypt

events.enhanced_description: The first known use of the Demotic script occurred around 664 BCE, marking a significant development in the writing systems of ancient Egypt. This script was used for a variety of documents, reflecting the cultural and administrative practices of the time.
events.name: First known use of the Demotic script

events.enhanced_description: The first known naval battle in Greek history took place between the city-states of Corinth and Corcyra around 664 BCE. This conflict marked a significant moment in the development of naval warfare in ancient Greece.
events.name: First naval battle in Greek recorded history, between Corinth and Corcyra

events.enhanced_description: In 664 BCE, Tantamani ascended to the throne as the king of Kush, succeeding his uncle Taharqa. This transition of power was significant for the Kushite dynasty during a time of conflict with the Assyrian Empire.
events.name: Tantamani succeeds his uncle Taharqa as king of Kush

events.enhanced_description: The Kushites launched an invasion of Assyrian-controlled Egypt around 664 BCE, seeking to reclaim their influence in the region. This invasion was part of the ongoing power struggles between the Kushite kingdom and the Assyrian Empire.
events.name: Kushites invade Assyrian-controlled Egypt

events.enhanced_description: In 664 BCE, the Assyrians, commanded by King Ashurbanipal, captured and sacked Thebes, a prominent city in ancient Egypt. This event was a pivotal moment in the Assyrian campaign to dominate Egypt and eliminate the Nubian influence.
events.name: The Assyrians under Ashurbanipal capture and sack Thebes, Egypt

events.enhanced_description: Psamtik I succeeded Necho I as the ruler of Lower Egypt around 664 BCE, marking the beginning of the 26th Dynasty. His reign is noted for the restoration of Egyptian power and culture after a period of foreign domination.
events.name: Psamtik I succeeds Necho I as ruler of Lower Egypt

events.enhanced_description: In 664 BCE, a solar superstorm occurred, which has been recorded in tree rings. This event is significant for understanding the impact of solar activity on Earth's climate and its historical implications.
events.name: Solar superstorm in 664 BCE recorded in tree rings

events.enhanced_description: In 663 BCE, the Assyrian Empire, led by King Ashurbanipal, successfully drove the Kushites out of Egypt, solidifying Assyrian control over the region. This military campaign was part of a broader strategy to maintain Assyrian dominance in the Near East.
events.name: The Assyrian Empire under Ashurbanipal drives the Kushites from Egypt

events.enhanced_description: The Siege of Tyre, which occurred in 663 BCE, was a significant military campaign led by the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal. This siege aimed to capture the strategic coastal city of Tyre, which was vital for trade and military operations in the region.
events.name: Siege of Tyre by the Assyrians under Ashurbanipal

events.enhanced_description: The traditional founding date of Japan is celebrated on February 11, marking the ascension of Emperor Jimmu, the legendary first emperor of Japan. This date symbolizes the beginning of the Japanese imperial line and the establishment of the nation.
events.name: Traditional founding date of Japan by Emperor Jimmu

events.enhanced_description: The mythical founding of the Japanese royal family is traditionally dated to 660 BCE with the ascension of Emperor Jimmu. This event is significant in Japanese history as it establishes the divine origin of the imperial lineage.
events.name: Mythical founding of the Japanese royal family

events.enhanced_description: The Spring and Autumn Annals documented the sighting of five meteors on December 24 in what is now Shanqiu County, marking a significant early observation in Chinese astronomy. This record showcases the historical attention to celestial events in ancient China.
events.name: Five meteors seen in the sky over Shanqiu

events.enhanced_description: The Spring and Autumn Annals recorded the first known observation of meteors in China, noting that five meteors were seen on December 24. This event marks an important moment in the history of astronomy in ancient China.
events.name: First Chinese observation of meteors

events.enhanced_description: The interregnum in Rome concludes as Ancus Marcius becomes king, known for his efforts to expand the city and strengthen its defenses, as well as for establishing religious practices.
events.name: Interregnum Ends with Ancus Marcius

events.enhanced_description: Cylon, an Athenian nobleman, attempts to take control of the Acropolis in a failed bid for kingship, leading to significant political repercussions in Athens.
events.name: Cylon's Failed Coup

events.enhanced_description: The establishment of Cyrene, a Greek colony in North Africa, represents a key moment in the spread of Hellenic culture and trade across the Mediterranean.
events.name: Cyrene Founded

events.enhanced_description: The interregnum in Rome concludes with Ancus Marcius ascending to the throne, becoming the fourth king of Rome. His reign is noted for expanding Roman territory and establishing important religious and political institutions.
events.name: Ancus Marcius Becomes King of Rome

events.enhanced_description: Sadyattes ascended to the throne of Lydia, continuing the legacy of his predecessor. His reign was characterized by military campaigns and efforts to consolidate power in Western Anatolia.
events.name: Sadyattes Becomes King of Lydia

events.enhanced_description: Duke Wen of Jin rises to power during the Zhou dynasty, marking a significant shift in the political landscape of ancient China. His leadership is noted for consolidating power and expanding the state's influence.
events.name: Duke Wen of Jin Ascends to Power

events.enhanced_description: Alyattes ascended to the throne of Lydia, succeeding his father, Sadyattes. His reign is marked by territorial expansion and the establishment of Lydia as a significant power in the ancient Near East.
events.name: Alyattes Becomes King of Lydia

events.enhanced_description: Cylon, an Athenian noble, attempts to seize control of the Acropolis in a failed coup, which ultimately leads to significant political strife in Athens and the eventual establishment of more democratic governance.
events.name: Cylon's Attempt to Seize the Acropolis

events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Chengpu, the State of Jin, led by Duke Wen, achieved a decisive victory over the State of Chu. This battle was crucial in establishing Jin's dominance in the region and showcased the military prowess of Duke Wen.
events.name: Battle of Chengpu

events.enhanced_description: The Greek colony of Cyrene is founded in present-day Libya, marking a significant expansion of Greek influence into North Africa. This settlement becomes an important center of trade and culture in the region.
events.name: Founding of Cyrene

events.enhanced_description: The Orientalizing period of Greek pottery, which saw the influence of Eastern art styles, came to an end around 625 BC. This transition marked a shift towards more distinctively Greek artistic expressions, paving the way for the subsequent Archaic period.
events.name: End of the Orientalizing Period of Vases

events.enhanced_description: Around 623 BC, Sin-shar-ishkun ascends to the throne of Assyria, succeeding his brother Assur-etel-ilani. This transition marks a significant moment in Assyrian history during a time of political instability and conflict.
events.name: Sin-shar-ishkun Succeeds Assur-etel-ilani

events.enhanced_description: The death of Ji Zheng, also known as King Xuan of Zhou, marked a pivotal moment in the history of the Zhou dynasty, leading to a power struggle that would affect the stability of the dynasty. His reign was characterized by efforts to strengthen the central authority of the Zhou.
events.name: Death of Ji Zheng, king of the Zhou dynasty of China

events.enhanced_description: Theophrastus, a Greek philosopher and botanist, documented the discovery of silphium, a plant valued for its medicinal properties, in the ancient city of Cyrene. This discovery highlighted the importance of Cyrene as a center of botanical knowledge in the ancient world.
events.name: Silphium discovered in Cyrene according to Theophrastus

events.enhanced_description: Ji Renchen, who became king during a turbulent period in the Zhou dynasty, faced challenges in maintaining the authority of the Zhou amidst rising regional powers. His reign is often seen as part of the larger narrative of the decline of the Zhou dynasty.
events.name: Ji Renchen becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China

events.enhanced_description: Lucius Tarquinius Priscus, an influential figure in Roman history, became the fifth king of Rome, known for his contributions to the city's infrastructure and military organization. His reign set the stage for the expansion of Roman power and influence.
events.name: Lucius Tarquinius Priscus becomes the fifth King of Rome

events.enhanced_description: The ancient city of Assur was sacked by a coalition of Medes and Babylonians, contributing to the decline of the Assyrian Empire. This event exemplified the growing power of the Medes and Babylonians as they sought to expand their territories at the expense of Assyria.
events.name: Sack of Assur by the Medes and Babylonians

events.enhanced_description: The death of Ji Renchen marked a significant transition in the Zhou dynasty, impacting the political landscape of ancient China. His reign was characterized by the ongoing challenges faced by the Zhou as they navigated power struggles with neighboring states.
events.name: Death of Ji Renchen, King of the Zhou Dynasty of China

events.enhanced_description: Ji Ban's ascension to the throne of the Zhou dynasty occurred during a period of significant political turmoil, where the authority of the Zhou kings was increasingly challenged by regional powers. His reign is often viewed as part of the broader narrative of the Zhou dynasty's decline.
events.name: Ji Ban Becomes King of the Zhou Dynasty of China

events.enhanced_description: The Neo-Babylonian kingdom's military campaigns against Assyrian cities marked the beginning of a significant conflict that would result in the eventual collapse of the Assyrian Empire. This period is characterized by shifting power dynamics in the ancient Near East.
events.name: Neo-Babylonian kingdom begin attacking Assyrian cities

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Nineveh saw a coalition of Medes, Persians, Scythians, Babylonians, and Susianians successfully besiege and conquer the Assyrian capital, Nineveh. The defeat marked a decisive turning point in the struggle for dominance in the ancient Near East, leading to the fall of the Assyrian Empire.
events.name: An alliance of Medes, Persians, Scythians, Babylonians and Susianians besiege and conquer Nineveh at the Battle of Nineveh

events.enhanced_description: Ashur-uballit II's efforts to maintain the remnants of the Assyrian Empire by establishing his rule in Harran represent a last-ditch attempt to preserve Assyrian sovereignty amid overwhelming external pressures. His reign is characterized by attempts to rally support against the advancing enemies.
events.name: Ashur-uballit II attempts to keep the Assyrian empire alive by establishing himself as king at Harran

events.enhanced_description: Lucius Tarquinius Priscus, a legendary figure in Roman history, ascended to the throne as the fifth king of Rome. His reign is attributed to significant developments in Roman society, including the establishment of important religious and political institutions.
events.name: Lucius Tarquinius Priscus becomes the legendary fifth king of Rome

events.enhanced_description: The Neo-Babylonian Empire initiated a series of military campaigns against Assyrian cities, signaling the start of a prolonged conflict that would lead to the eventual downfall of the Assyrian Empire. This aggressive expansion marked the rise of Babylonian power in the ancient Near East.
events.name: The Neo-Babylonian Empire begins attacking Assyrian cities

events.enhanced_description: The city of Assur, a key center of the Assyrian Empire, was sacked by an alliance of the Medes and Babylonians, marking a significant moment in the decline of Assyrian power. This event contributed to the eventual fall of the Assyrian Empire and the rise of Babylonian dominance in the region.
events.name: The Medes and Babylonians sack Assur

events.enhanced_description: King Zhuang of Chu, also known as Zhuang Wang, became the ruler of the state of Chu during the Eastern Zhou period of Chinese history. His reign is noted for the consolidation of power in the region and the expansion of Chu's influence over neighboring states.
events.name: King Zhuang of Chu ascends to the throne of Chu in China

events.enhanced_description: The Babylonians achieved a significant victory by defeating the Assyrian army led by Ashur-uballit II and capturing the city of Harran. This marked the decline of the Assyrian Empire and the rise of Babylonian power in the region.
events.name: Babylonians Capture Harran

events.enhanced_description: Halley's Comet was observed from Earth between March 15 and March 26, marking a significant astronomical event. Its visibility was recorded by ancient civilizations and contributed to the understanding of comets in history.
events.name: Visibility of Halley's Comet

events.enhanced_description: Ji Yu succeeded Zhou Kuang Wang as king of the Zhou dynasty in China, continuing the legacy of the Zhou rulers. His reign is part of a complex period in Chinese history characterized by feudalism and the rise of various states.
events.name: Ji Yu Becomes King of Zhou Dynasty

events.enhanced_description: In a significant military engagement, Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon defeated the forces of Necho II of Egypt at the Battle of Carchemish. This victory was crucial for the Babylonian conquest of Assyria and established Babylonian dominance in the region.
events.name: Battle of Carchemish (Second Mention)

events.enhanced_description: Following the Battle of Carchemish, Nebuchadnezzar II secured another victory against the Egyptian forces at Hamath. This battle further solidified Babylonian control over the former Assyrian territories and marked the decline of Egyptian influence in the region.
events.name: Battle of Hamath (Second Mention)

events.enhanced_description: Nebuchadnezzar II ascended to the throne of Babylon following the death of his father, Nabopolassar, marking the beginning of a significant era in Babylonian history. His reign is noted for military conquests and monumental building projects, including the famed Hanging Gardens, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
events.name: Nebuchadnezzar II succeeds his father Nabopolassar as King of Babylon

events.enhanced_description: Perinthus was established by Greek settlers from Samos, serving as a vital trade hub in the region. The city played an important role in the cultural and economic exchanges between the Greeks and the local populations.

events.name: Foundation of Perinthus by settlers from Samos (traditional date)

events.enhanced_description: The Jewish–Babylonian War marked the beginning of hostilities between the Kingdom of Judah and the Babylonian Empire, leading to significant territorial and political changes in the region. This conflict ultimately contributed to the Babylonian Exile of the Jewish people.

events.name: The Jewish–Babylonian war begins between the Kingdom of Judah and Babylonia

events.enhanced_description: Founded by Greek settlers from Phocaea, Marseille quickly became a prominent trading port in the Mediterranean. Its establishment is a significant event in the spread of Greek culture and trade throughout the region, particularly in relation to the Carthaginians.
events.name: Marseille is founded by Greeks of Phocaea

events.enhanced_description: The establishment of the Satrapy of Armenia marked the incorporation of the region into the Persian Empire, reflecting the administrative strategies of the Achaemenid dynasty. This move significantly influenced the political landscape of the region for centuries to come.
events.name: The Satrapy of Armenia is created

events.enhanced_description: The founding of Capua marked the establishment of one of the most important cities in ancient Italy, which would later play a significant role in the Roman Republic. Its strategic location contributed to its growth as a center of trade and culture.
events.name: Capua is founded

events.enhanced_description: Alyattes, the Lydian king, led a campaign against Smyrna, resulting in the city's destruction. This event exemplified the shifting power dynamics in the region and the conflicts between emerging powers in Anatolia.
events.name: Smyrna is sacked and destroyed by Alyattes of Lydia

events.enhanced_description: The construction of the Hanging Gardens of Babylon, attributed to Nebuchadnezzar II, is one of the most famous architectural achievements of the ancient world. Although its existence has been debated, it symbolizes the grandeur of Babylonian civilization and its advancements in engineering and horticulture.
events.name: Nebuchadnezzar II builds the Hanging Gardens of Babylon

events.enhanced_description: Halley's Comet was visible from Earth from March 15 through March 26, making a close approach to our planet. This event was noted by ancient astronomers and is significant in the study of historical astronomy.
events.name: Halley's Comet Visible

events.enhanced_description: King Ding succeeded his father, King Kuang, as the ruler of the Zhou dynasty in China. His reign marked a continuation of the Zhou dynasty's influence in Chinese history during a period of significant political and social change.
events.name: King Ding of Zhou Succeeds King Kuang of Zhou

events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Carchemish, Crown Prince Nebuchadnezzar II led the Babylonian forces to a decisive victory over the allied armies of Egypt and Assyria. This battle was crucial for Babylon's dominance in the region and marked the beginning of the Babylonian conquest of Assyria.
events.name: Battle of Carchemish

events.enhanced_description: Following his victory at Carchemish, Nebuchadnezzar II defeated the remaining Egyptian forces at the Battle of Hamath. This battle further solidified Babylonian power in the region and eliminated the last significant resistance from Egypt.
events.name: Battle of Hamath

events.enhanced_description: Nebuchadnezzar II ascended to the throne of Babylonia following the death of his father, Nabopolassar. His reign is noted for military conquests and the expansion of the Babylonian Empire, as well as significant architectural achievements.
events.name: Nebuchadnezzar II Becomes King of Babylonia

events.enhanced_description: In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar II declared an intercalary month, Ululu II, which began on September 6. This event is significant in the context of Babylonian calendar reforms and reflects the administrative practices of the time.
events.name: Proclamation of Intercalary Month by Nebuchadnezzar II

events.enhanced_description: The Babylonian New Year, Nisannu 1, is celebrated on January 14-15, marking the beginning of the agricultural year in ancient Babylon. This festival was accompanied by various rituals and festivities that were central to Babylonian culture.
events.name: Babylonian New Year of Nisannu 1

events.enhanced_description: According to tradition, Perinthus was founded by settlers from the island of Samos. This ancient city, located on the Thracian coast of the Sea of Marmara, became an important center of trade and culture in the region.
events.name: Foundation of Perinthus

events.enhanced_description: The Jewish–Babylonian War marks the beginning of hostilities between the Kingdom of Judah and the Babylonian Empire, culminating in the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BCE. This conflict was pivotal in shaping the history of the Jewish people and their subsequent exile.
events.name: Jewish–Babylonian War Begins

events.enhanced_description: The founding of Milan by Celtic tribes around the 6th century BCE marked the establishment of one of Italy's most important cities, known as Mediolanum in ancient times. This event set the stage for Milan's future as a major cultural and economic center in the region.
events.name: Milan is founded by Celts

events.enhanced_description: The founding of Pompeii around the 6th century BCE marks the beginning of a city that would later become famous for its preservation under volcanic ash. Initially settled by the Oscans, Pompeii would evolve into a vibrant Roman city before its tragic destruction in 79 CE.
events.name: Pompeii is founded

events.enhanced_description: The Etruscan capture of Rome transformed it into a prosperous trading center, significantly influencing its early development. This event set the stage for Rome's later growth into a major power in the Mediterranean.
events.name: The Etruscans capture the settlement of Rome

events.enhanced_description: The rise of Zarathustra's teachings marked a significant shift in religious thought in ancient Persia, leading to the establishment of Zoroastrianism as a major world religion. Its dualistic cosmology and ethical teachings influenced later religious traditions.

image.caption: Faravahar symbol on the Fire Temple in Yazd, Iran.
image.date_qualification: Photographed 2016-10-23; this is not the date of the historical event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Zarathustra's religion becomes popular in Persia

events.enhanced_description: The construction of the Temple of Artemis on the island of Corfu represents a significant architectural achievement of the ancient Greeks. This temple would later be recognized for its artistic and cultural importance in the Hellenistic period.
events.name: Construction begins on the Temple of Artemis, Korkyra (Corfu)

events.enhanced_description: The construction of the largest mound at Cahokia signifies the rise of one of the most complex pre-Columbian societies in North America. This monumental earthwork reflects the social and political organization of the Cahokian culture.
events.name: Construction begins on the largest mound at Cahokia

events.enhanced_description: Jeconiah succeeded his father Jehoiakim as King of Judah during a tumultuous period marked by external pressures from powerful empires. His reign was short-lived, reflecting the instability of the region during the Babylonian conquest.
events.name: Jeconiah Succeeds Jehoiakim

events.enhanced_description: Psamtik II succeeded Necho II as the king of Egypt, continuing the legacy of the 26th Dynasty. His reign was marked by military campaigns and efforts to maintain Egypt's influence in the region.
events.name: Psamtik II Succeeds Necho II

events.enhanced_description: The First Sacred War began in ancient Greece, primarily centered around the control of the sanctuary at Delphi. This conflict highlighted the tensions between various Greek city-states and their religious affiliations, setting the stage for future military engagements.
events.name: Beginning of the First Sacred War

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Bi was fought between the State of Jin and the State of Chu, with the Jin forces led by Viscount Huan suffering a significant defeat. This battle is an important event in the context of the power struggles during the Zhou dynasty in ancient China.
events.name: Battle of Bi

events.enhanced_description: The poet Sappho returned from her exile in Sicily, a significant moment in her life that allowed her to continue her literary contributions to ancient Greek culture. Her poetry, celebrated for its emotional depth and lyrical beauty, has had a lasting impact on literature.
events.name: Sappho Returns from Exile

events.enhanced_description: Amidst an economic crisis and social unrest, the leaders of Athens appointed the poet-statesman Solon to implement democratic reforms. His policies laid the groundwork for future democratic governance in Athens, marking a pivotal moment in the city's political evolution.
events.name: Solon's Appointment in Athens

events.enhanced_description: Solon established the Ecclesia, the principal assembly of democracy in Athens, during its Golden Age. This assembly empowered citizens to participate in governance, a revolutionary step in the development of democratic ideals.
events.name: Establishment of the Ecclesia

events.enhanced_description: The sacking of Napata by Egyptian forces led to the collapse of the Kushite capital and the subsequent relocation of the Kushite court to Meroë. This event signifies the decline of Kushite power and the increasing dominance of Egypt in the region.
events.name: Napata Sacked by Egyptians

events.enhanced_description: An Egyptian military force sacked the city of Napata, leading to the relocation of the Cushite court to Meroë. This event marked a significant shift in power and influence in the region, as the Cushites sought safety from Egyptian aggression.
events.name: Egyptian Sack of Napata

events.enhanced_description: The invasion of the Kingdom of Urartu by the Medians resulted in the fall of this once-powerful kingdom. This event exemplifies the shifting power dynamics in the region during the late 7th century BCE, contributing to the rise of the Medes as a significant force in ancient history.
events.name: Medians Invade Urartu

events.enhanced_description: Apries ascended to the throne of Egypt following the reign of his father, Psamtik II, marking a continuation of the 26th Dynasty. His reign was characterized by military campaigns and economic challenges, reflecting the complexities of governance in ancient Egypt.
events.name: Apries Succeeds Psamtik II

events.enhanced_description: Nebuchadnezzar II began his siege of Jerusalem, a pivotal event that led to the Babylonian conquest of the city and the subsequent exile of the Jewish population. This siege marked a significant turning point in Jewish history and the rise of Babylonian power.
events.name: Nebuchadnezzar's Siege of Jerusalem

events.enhanced_description: The founding of Akragas, later known as Agrigento, marked the establishment of one of Sicily's most important ancient Greek cities. It became known for its rich culture and impressive temples, contributing to the Hellenistic heritage of the island.
events.name: Foundation of Akragas

events.enhanced_description: The destruction of Kirrha marked the end of the First Sacred War, a conflict primarily fought over control of the sanctuary at Delphi. This event underscored the tensions between various Greek city-states and their religious sites, reflecting the intertwining of warfare and sacred spaces in ancient Greece.
events.name: Destruction of Kirrha

events.enhanced_description: The Kingdom of Urartu fell following a Median invasion, marking a significant shift in power in the region. This event contributed to the decline of Urartian influence and the rise of neighboring powers, including the Medes and later the Persians.
events.name: Fall of the Kingdom of Urartu

events.enhanced_description: Croesus became the king of Lydia, succeeding his father Alyattes, and is often remembered for his immense wealth and the eventual downfall of his kingdom to Cyrus the Great of Persia. His reign marked a significant period in Lydian history, known for its economic prosperity and cultural achievements.
events.name: Croesus Succeeds Alyattes as King of Lydia

events.enhanced_description: A significant military clash occurred between the ancient powers of Egypt and Babylon around 585 BC, reflecting the ongoing struggles for dominance in the region. This conflict highlighted the geopolitical tensions of the time and the shifting alliances among these powerful states.
events.name: Military Clash Between Egypt and Babylon

events.enhanced_description: King Ding was a ruler of the Zhou dynasty, and his death marked a significant transition in the dynasty's history. His reign was characterized by internal strife and challenges to Zhou authority, which would lead to further fragmentation of power in China.
events.name: Death of King Ding of the Zhou dynasty of China

events.enhanced_description: Lucius Tarquinius Priscus, the fifth king of Rome, achieved a significant military victory against the Sabines, capturing the town of Collatia. Following his triumph, he celebrated with a grand procession, which was a traditional Roman honor for victorious generals.
events.name: Lucius Tarquinius Priscus' Triumph over the Sabines

events.enhanced_description: Ji Yi's ascension to the throne as King Jian of the Zhou dynasty marked a new chapter in the dynasty's history. His reign would be characterized by the ongoing challenges faced by the Zhou as they struggled to maintain control over their territories amidst rising regional powers.
events.name: Ji Yi becomes King Jian of the Zhou dynasty of China

events.enhanced_description: Nebuchadnezzar II ordered the third deportation of Jews from Judah to Babylon, a pivotal event in Jewish history that marked the beginning of the Babylonian Exile. This deportation had profound effects on Jewish culture and identity.
events.name: Third Deportation of Jews from Judah

events.enhanced_description: The Pythian Games, one of the four Panhellenic Games of ancient Greece, were reorganized at Delphi, reflecting the cultural significance of the site as a center for worship and competition. This event contributed to the enduring legacy of the Games in Greek culture.
events.name: Reorganization of the Pythian Games at Delphi

events.enhanced_description: Suizei's ascension as the second Emperor of Japan marked a foundational moment in Japanese history, establishing the imperial lineage that would continue for centuries. His reign is part of the legendary period of Japanese history.
events.name: Suizei becomes the second Emperor of Japan

events.enhanced_description: Astyages succeeded Cyaxares as the king of the Medes, continuing the legacy of the Median Empire. His reign would later be marked by conflicts with the rising power of the Persian Empire, shaping the political landscape of the region.
events.name: Astyages succeeds Cyaxares as king of the Medes

events.enhanced_description: In 585 BC, a solar eclipse occurred during a battle between Alyattes of Lydia and Cyaxares of Media at the Halys River, leading to a truce between the two powers. This event is notable not only for its military implications but also for its astronomical significance, as it helped establish a timeline for future historical events.
events.name: Solar Eclipse during the Battle of Halys River

events.enhanced_description: On September 13, Lucius Tarquinius Priscus, the fifth king of Rome, achieved a significant military victory over the Sabines, capturing the town of Collatia and celebrating a grand triumph. This event reinforced his authority and the growing power of the Roman monarchy during this period.
events.name: Lucius Tarquinius Priscus' Triumph

events.enhanced_description: The Isthmian Games were founded at Corinth, adding to the rich tradition of athletic competitions in ancient Greece. These games honored the sea god Poseidon and became a significant cultural event in the Greek calendar.
events.name: Foundation of the Isthmian Games at Corinth

events.enhanced_description: Cambyses I succeeded Cyrus I as king of Anshan, continuing the legacy of the Achaemenid dynasty. His reign set the stage for the future expansion of the Persian Empire under his son, Cyrus the Great.
events.name: Cambyses I succeeds Cyrus I as king of Anshan

events.enhanced_description: The Gorgon Medusa, a striking detail from the west pediment of the Temple of Artemis on the island of Corfu, represents a significant example of ancient Greek sculpture. This work reflects the artistic style and cultural values of the time, particularly the fascination with mythological themes.
events.name: Gorgon Medusa Sculpture

events.enhanced_description: The Standing Youth, known as a kouros, is a significant representation of ancient Greek art that embodies the ideals of youth and beauty. This sculpture is notable for its rigid stance and stylized features, characteristic of the Archaic period.
events.name: Standing Youth (Kouros) Sculpture

events.enhanced_description: The Berlin Kore, a significant example of Archaic Greek sculpture, was initiated in a cemetery near Keratea, showcasing the evolving artistic styles of the time. This statue is now housed in the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, reflecting the cultural exchanges of the era.
events.name: Berlin Kore is begun

events.enhanced_description: The establishment of the Satrapy of Armenia marked the incorporation of the region into the Achaemenid Empire, signifying the expansion of Persian influence. This event laid the groundwork for the historical identity of Armenia within the context of empires.
events.name: The Satrapy of Armenia is established as a province of the Achaemenid Empire

events.enhanced_description: The Francois Vase, an exquisite example of black-figure pottery, was created by the artists Kleitias and Ergotimos. This work is celebrated for its intricate decoration and storytelling, representing a high point in ancient Greek ceramic art.
events.name: Francois Vase is made by Kleitias and Ergotimos

events.enhanced_description: Amasis II successfully overthrew Apries, reclaiming the throne of Egypt and initiating a new era of stability and prosperity. His reign is noted for its cultural achievements and the strengthening of Egypt's economy and military.
events.name: Amasis II drives Apries from the throne of Egypt

events.enhanced_description: Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, renounced worldly life and took Diksha (initiation) in Vaishali, marking a pivotal moment in the development of Jain philosophy and spirituality. His teachings emphasized non-violence, truth, and asceticism, which became foundational to Jain beliefs.
events.name: The 24th Jain Tirthankara, Mahavira, takes Diksha

events.enhanced_description: Deposed pharaoh Apries attempted to reclaim his throne by invading Egypt with the support of Babylonian forces, but he was ultimately defeated by Amasis II. This conflict underscored the political turmoil and foreign influence affecting Egypt during this era.
events.name: Deposed pharaoh Apries invades Egypt with Babylonian help but is defeated by Amasis II

events.enhanced_description: Servius Tullius, the sixth king of Rome, celebrated a grand triumph in honor of his military victories against the Etruscans. This event not only demonstrated his military prowess but also reinforced his authority and legitimacy as a ruler in the early Roman Kingdom.
events.name: Servius Tullius celebrates a triumph for his victory over the Etruscans

events.enhanced_description: The inaugural Panathenaic Games were celebrated in Athens, establishing a tradition that would continue for centuries and become one of the most significant athletic festivals in ancient Greece. These games honored the goddess Athena and included various athletic competitions, showcasing the cultural importance of sport in Greek society.
events.name: The first known Panathenaic Games of Ancient Greece are held in Athens

events.enhanced_description: The first known Panathenaic Games were conducted in Athens, establishing a tradition that would continue for centuries and become one of the most significant athletic festivals in ancient Greece. These games honored the goddess Athena and included various athletic competitions, showcasing the cultural importance of sport in Greek society.
events.name: The first known Panathenaic Games of Ancient Greece are conducted in Athens

events.enhanced_description: Vardhamana, later known as Mahavira, attained Enlightenment, marking a pivotal moment in the history of Jainism. His teachings and philosophies would lay the foundation for one of the major religions in India, emphasizing non-violence and truth.
events.name: Vardhamana attained True Knowledge and became Mahavira

events.enhanced_description: Amel-Marduk, also known as Evil-Merodach, ascended to the throne of Babylon following the death of his father, Nebuchadnezzar II. His reign was marked by a brief period of relative peace and the release of prisoners, but it was also characterized by instability and eventual overthrow.
events.name: Amel-Marduk succeeds Nebuchadnezzar II as king of Babylon

events.enhanced_description: Neriglissar took the throne of Babylon after Amel-Marduk, marking another transition in the leadership of this ancient civilization. His reign was characterized by efforts to restore Babylon's power following a period of turmoil and instability.
events.name: Neriglissar succeeds Amel-Marduk as king of Babylon

events.enhanced_description: Amtalqa ascended to the throne of Kush following the reign of his brother Aspelta, marking a significant transition in the leadership of this ancient African kingdom. The Kingdom of Kush, located to the south of Egypt, was known for its rich resources and powerful rulers.
events.name: Amtalqa succeeds his brother Aspelta as king of Kush

events.enhanced_description: Apries, the deposed pharaoh of Egypt, attempted to reclaim his throne with the assistance of Babylonian forces but faced a decisive defeat at the hands of Amasis II, the Saite pharaoh. This conflict highlighted the political instability in Egypt during this period and the shifting power dynamics between local and foreign rulers.
events.name: Former pharaoh Apries invades Egypt with Babylonian help but is defeated by Saite pharaoh Amasis II

events.enhanced_description: In a rare astronomical event, all eight planets of the Solar System, along with the dwarf planet Pluto, aligned in a unique formation. This alignment captured the interest of astronomers and stargazers alike, showcasing the dynamic nature of celestial bodies in our solar system.
events.name: All eight planets of the Solar System as well as the dwarf planet Pluto fall into planetary alignment

events.enhanced_description: Pisistratus, an aristocrat, seized control of the Acropolis in Athens and declared himself tyrant, initiating a period of significant political change in the city-state. His rule is noted for both tyranny and advancements in civic culture, leading to a complex legacy in Athenian history.
events.name: Pisistratus seizes the Acropolis of Athens and declares himself tyrant

events.enhanced_description: Croesus ascended to the throne of Lydia, marking the beginning of a prosperous reign known for its wealth and the development of coinage. His rule is often associated with the height of Lydian power and culture, as well as interactions with neighboring states such as Persia and Greece.
events.name: Croesus becomes king of Lydia

events.enhanced_description: Peisistratus seized control of the Acropolis in Athens around 560 BCE, establishing himself as the city's tyrant for the first time. His rule would significantly influence Athenian politics and culture in the years to come.
events.name: Peisistratus Seizes the Acropolis

events.enhanced_description: The Calf Bearer, a significant Archaic Greek statue, was created around 560 BCE and is now displayed at the Acropolis Museum in Athens. This sculpture reflects the artistic developments of the period and the cultural practices of ancient Greece.
events.name: Calf Bearer (Moscophoros) Created

events.enhanced_description: The Berlin Kore, a notable example of Archaic Greek sculpture, was completed around 560 BCE. This statue is now housed in the Altes Museum in Berlin and represents the artistic achievements of the period.
events.name: Berlin Kore Finished

events.enhanced_description: The Calf Bearer, a significant statue from ancient Greece, was completed during this period, representing the artistic achievements of the time. This statue is notable for its depiction of a man carrying a calf, symbolizing devotion and sacrifice, and is an important artifact of Archaic Greek art.
events.name: The statue known as The Calf Bearer (Moschophoros) is completed

events.enhanced_description: The statue known as The Calf Bearer (Moschophoros) was completed, representing a significant artistic achievement in ancient Greek sculpture. This work exemplifies the transition towards more naturalistic representations in art during this period.
events.name: The Calf Bearer (Moschophoros) statue is completed

events.enhanced_description: Cyrus the Great succeeded his father, Cambyses I, as the ruler of Anshan around 559 BCE. This succession marked the beginning of Cyrus's rise to power, which would eventually lead to the establishment of the vast Persian Empire.
events.name: Cyrus the Great Succeeds Cambyses I

events.enhanced_description: In 559 BCE, the Babylonian king Neriglissar declared an intercalendary month, a significant administrative decision that affected the calendar and agricultural practices in Babylon. This declaration marked the beginning of his first year of kingship, which started on Nisan 1.
events.name: Neriglissar Declares Intercalendary Month

events.enhanced_description: Hegesias was removed from his position as Archon of Athens around 558 BCE, a political move that reflected the turbulent nature of Athenian governance during this period.
events.name: Hegesias Removed as Archon of Athens

events.enhanced_description: The state of Jin achieved a significant military victory over its rival state of Qin in a battle around 558 BCE, showcasing the ongoing conflicts among the Chinese states during the Spring and Autumn period.
events.name: Jin Defeats Qin in Battle

events.enhanced_description: In 557 BCE, the Persians laid siege to the city of Larissa (Calah), but their initial attempts to capture it were unsuccessful. However, a solar eclipse caused panic among the inhabitants, leading to their abandonment of the city, which allowed the Persians to take control.
events.name: Persians Besiege Larissa

events.enhanced_description: Labashi-Marduk's reign as king of Babylon began around 557 BCE after succeeding Neriglissar. His rule was characterized by instability and was short-lived, as he was quickly followed by Nabonidus.
events.name: Labashi-Marduk's Reign as King of Babylon

events.enhanced_description: Labashi-Marduk ascended to the throne of Babylon following the reign of Neriglissar, marking a brief period in Babylonian history around 556 BCE. His reign was short-lived, as he was soon succeeded by Nabonidus, who would rule for a much longer period.
events.name: Labashi-Marduk Becomes King of Babylon

events.enhanced_description: Pisistratus, a prominent figure in Athenian politics, was expelled to Euboea around 556 BCE after facing opposition in Athens. During his exile, he capitalized on the wealth from Thrace's mines, which would later aid in his return to power.
events.name: Pisistratus Expelled to Euboea

events.enhanced_description: Nabonidus became the king of Babylon following the brief reign of Labashi-Marduk around 556 BCE. His reign is noted for its religious reforms and his unusual focus on the worship of the moon god Sin, which set him apart from his predecessors.

image.caption: Detail of a stele depicting Nabonidus in traditional Babylonian royal dress, holding objects symbolizing justice and power.
image.credit: Osama Shukir Muhammed Amin FRCP(Glasg) — Own work

events.name: Nabonidus Succeeds Labashi-Marduk

events.enhanced_description: Cyrus II, later known as Cyrus the Great, initiated a revolt against his grandfather Astyages, the king of the Medes, around 553 BCE. This revolt was a significant turning point that led to the establishment of the Persian Empire, as Cyrus would go on to conquer Media and expand his territory.
events.name: Cyrus II Revolts Against Astyages

events.enhanced_description: Siddhartha Gautama, after years of rigorous meditation and penance, attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya, India, around the 6th century BCE. This pivotal moment marked the founding of Buddhism, a major world religion that emphasizes the path to enlightenment through ethical living, meditation, and wisdom.
events.name: Founding of Buddhism

events.enhanced_description: Cyrus the Great launched a military campaign against Babylonia, which was pivotal in establishing Persian control over the region and reshaping the political landscape of the ancient Near East.
events.name: Cyrus attacks Babylonia

events.enhanced_description: The founding of the Greek city of Elea in southern Italy marked an important development in the spread of Greek culture and civilization in the region, contributing to the rich tapestry of ancient Italian history.
events.name: Greek city of Elea is founded

events.enhanced_description: The conquest of the Lycian city of Xanthos by the Persians represented a significant military achievement, further extending Persian influence over the region of Lycia in southwestern Anatolia.
events.name: Persians conquer Lycian city of Xanthos

events.enhanced_description: The Amasis Painter created a notable black-figure decoration on an amphora depicting Dionysos with maenads, showcasing the artistic achievements of ancient Greek pottery and the cultural significance of Dionysian themes.
events.name: Amasis Painter creates Dionysos with maenads

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Opis was a decisive conflict in which the forces of the Persian Achaemenid Empire, led by Cyrus the Great, defeated the troops of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, solidifying Persian dominance in the region.
events.name: Battle of Opis

events.enhanced_description: The Fall of Babylon occurred when Achaemenid troops under Gobryas entered the city without opposition, leading to the incorporation of the Neo-Babylonian Empire into the Achaemenid Empire under Cyrus the Great, marking a significant expansion of Persian power.
events.name: Fall of Babylon

events.enhanced_description: The end of the Babylonian captivity occurred when Cyrus the Great, king of Persia, permitted the Jews to return to Jerusalem, leading to the leadership of Zerubbabel and Joshua the High Priest in the reconstruction of their temple.
events.name: The Babylonian captivity of the Jews ends

events.enhanced_description: The laying of the foundations for the Second Temple in Jerusalem marked a pivotal moment in Jewish history, symbolizing the return from Babylonian exile and the restoration of religious practices.
events.name: The Jews lay the foundations for the Second Temple

events.enhanced_description: Phrynaeus was appointed as the archon of Athens, a significant political position in the city-state. His leadership came during a transformative period in Athenian governance and society.
events.name: Phrynaeus is appointed archon of Athens

events.enhanced_description: The Sungai Batu Civilization, one of the earliest known civilizations in Malaysia, began during this period. It is notable for its advanced trade networks and cultural developments in the region.
events.name: The Sungai Batu Civilization in Malaysia begins

events.enhanced_description: Lucius Tarquinius Superbus ascended to the throne as the seventh king of Rome after the assassination of his predecessor, Servius Tullius. His reign was marked by tyranny and was a significant factor leading to the establishment of the Roman Republic.
events.name: Lucius Tarquinius Superbus becomes the seventh king of Rome

events.enhanced_description: The City Dionysia festival in Athens introduced competitions for tragedy, which played a crucial role in the development of Greek theater and drama. This event marked the beginning of a tradition that would influence Western literature for centuries.
events.name: Competitions for tragedy are instituted at the City Dionysia festival in Athens

events.enhanced_description: The Etruscans established the city of Felsina, which would later evolve into the modern city of Bologna. This foundation marked an important development in the region's urban history and Etruscan influence in northern Italy.
events.name: The Etruscans founded the city of Felsina

events.enhanced_description: The Royal Arch Masons adopted the year 533 BCE as the starting point for their dating system, known as Anno Inventionis, which marks the beginning of the Second Temple period in Jerusalem, initiated by Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile.
events.name: Royal Arch Masons take this year as the epoch for dating their documents Anno Inventionis after the beginning of the Second Temple by Zerubbabel

events.enhanced_description: The State of Zhoulai was conquered by the State of Wu, marking a significant shift in power dynamics during the Eastern Zhou period in ancient China. This event exemplifies the intense rivalries and conflicts among the various states during the Spring and Autumn period.
events.name: Conquest of the State of Zhoulai by Wu

events.enhanced_description: Around 528 BC, Gautama Buddha attained Enlightenment while meditating under the Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya, India. This pivotal moment marked the beginning of his ministry and the foundation of Buddhism, which would grow to become one of the world's major religions.
events.name: Gautama Buddha's Enlightenment

events.enhanced_description: According to the Swetambara tradition, Jain Tirthankara Mahavira attained Moksha around 528 BC in Vaishali, India. This event is significant in Jainism as it represents the liberation of Mahavira's soul from the cycle of birth and death, marking the culmination of his spiritual journey.
events.name: Mahavira attains Moksha

events.enhanced_description: Peisistratos, a prominent tyrant of Athens, died around 528 BC, leading to his son Hippias inheriting his power. This transition marked a critical point in Athenian politics, as Hippias would later face challenges that would lead to the eventual establishment of democracy in Athens.
events.name: Hippias inherits power from Peisistratos

events.enhanced_description: Psammetichus III ascended to the throne of Egypt around 528 BC, succeeding Amasis II. His reign was marked by challenges from external powers, particularly the Persian Empire, which would soon lead to significant changes in Egyptian governance.
events.name: Psammetichus III becomes king of Egypt

events.enhanced_description: King Liao ascended to power in the State of Wu during the Zhou dynasty around 528 BC. His reign was part of a larger narrative of the Zhou dynasty's fragmentation and the rise of regional powers in ancient China.
events.name: King Liao ascends in the State of Wu

events.enhanced_description: Around 528 BC, Babylon rebelled against Persian rule, reflecting the growing discontent among conquered peoples. This rebellion was part of the larger context of resistance against the expanding Persian Empire.
events.name: Babylonian rebellion against Persian rule

events.enhanced_description: The Babylonian rebellion against Persian rule was suppressed around 528 BC, demonstrating the might of the Persian Empire under Darius I. This suppression solidified Persian control over Babylon and reinforced the empire's dominance in the region.
events.name: Suppression of the Babylonian rebellion

events.enhanced_description: Cleomenes I succeeded Anaxandridas as king of Sparta around 528 BC. His reign was marked by military campaigns and political maneuvers that would shape the future of Spartan power in Greece.
events.name: Cleomenes I becomes king of Sparta

events.enhanced_description: In 529 BC, Babylon staged a rebellion against Persian rule, reflecting the tensions and resistance faced by the Persian Empire in maintaining control over its vast territories. This event highlighted the challenges of governance in a diverse empire.
events.name: Babylon rebels against Persian rule

events.enhanced_description: The state of Zhoulai fell to the military might of the State of Wu, reflecting the ongoing conflicts among the various states during the Eastern Zhou period of Chinese history. This conquest contributed to the shifting power dynamics in the region.
events.name: The Chinese state of Zhoulai is conquered by Wu

events.enhanced_description: Around 527 BCE, Gautama Buddha attained Enlightenment under the Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya, India. This pivotal moment marked the beginning of his ministry, during which he would share his insights and teachings, laying the foundation for Buddhism.
events.name: Gautama Buddha attains Enlightenment and begins his ministry

events.enhanced_description: According to the Swetambara tradition of Jainism, Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, attained Moksha (liberation) at the age of 72 in Vaishali. His teachings and life have profoundly influenced Jain philosophy and ethics, emphasizing non-violence and truth.
events.name: Jain Tirthankara Mahavira attains Moksha

events.enhanced_description: Peisistratos, a significant figure in Athenian history known for his tyranny and reforms, died, leading to his son Hippias inheriting his power. This transition marked a pivotal moment in the political landscape of Athens, influencing its future democratic developments.
events.name: Peisistratos dies, Hippias inherits power

events.enhanced_description: Psammetichus III ascended to the throne of Egypt following the death of Amasis II, marking the continuation of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty. His reign would be short-lived as he faced the impending threat from the Persian Empire.
events.name: Psammetichus III succeeds Amasis II

events.enhanced_description: King Liao ascended to the throne of the State of Wu during the Zhou dynasty, a period marked by significant political fragmentation and warfare among various states in ancient China. His rule contributed to the historical narrative of the Warring States period.
events.name: King Liao of Wu ascends to power

events.enhanced_description: Around 528 BC, Cambyses II, the ruler of Persia, conquered Egypt, defeating Psammetichus III. This pivotal event marked the end of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty and the beginning of the Persian Twenty-seventh Dynasty, significantly altering the course of Egyptian history.
events.name: Cambyses II conquers Egypt

events.enhanced_description: Bardiya, also known as Smerdis, succeeded his brother Cambyses II as ruler of Persia. His ascent to the throne was marked by controversy and claims of usurpation, contributing to the complex narrative of Persian royal succession.
events.name: Bardiya succeeds Cambyses II

events.enhanced_description: Darius I ascended to the throne of Persia after the controversial rule of Bardiya. His reign marked the establishment of a stable and expansive Persian Empire, characterized by significant administrative reforms and military conquests.
events.name: Darius I succeeds Bardiya

events.enhanced_description: The rebellion in Babylon against Persian rule was ultimately suppressed, reaffirming Persian control over the region. This event underscored the challenges faced by the Persian Empire in maintaining its vast territories.
events.name: The Babylonian rebellion is suppressed

events.enhanced_description: Dao ascended to the throne as King of the Zhou dynasty but died within the same year, highlighting the instability of leadership during this tumultuous period in Chinese history. His brief reign is part of the larger narrative of the Zhou dynasty's decline.
events.name: Dao becomes King of the Zhou dynasty

events.enhanced_description: Cleomenes I succeeded Anaxandridas as king of Sparta, a city-state known for its military prowess and austere lifestyle. His reign would see significant developments in Spartan politics and military strategy.
events.name: Cleomenes I succeeds Anaxandridas

events.enhanced_description: In 525 BCE, the Battle of Pelusium marked the conquest of Egypt by Cambyses II of Persia. Utilizing psychological warfare by painting sacred animals on his soldiers' shields, Cambyses's forces instilled fear in the Egyptian defenders, leading to a swift victory.
events.name: Battle of Pelusium

events.enhanced_description: After the Battle of Pelusium in 525 BCE, Cambyses II captured the Egyptian Pharaoh Psamtik III. Initially treating him with respect, Cambyses executed him when Psamtik attempted to incite a revolt, demonstrating the harsh realities of power in the ancient world.
events.name: Cambyses takes Psamtik III prisoner

events.enhanced_description: The year 525 BCE marked the end of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt and the rise of the Twenty-seventh Dynasty under Persian rule. This transition was a pivotal moment in Egyptian history, leading to significant changes in governance and culture.
events.name: The Twenty-sixth Dynasty ends, and the Twenty-seventh Dynasty begins

events.enhanced_description: After conquering Egypt in 525 BCE, Cambyses II sent ambassadors to the Macrobians, seeking their submission through lavish gifts. The Macrobian king's challenge to Cambyses, symbolized by an unstrung bow, highlighted the tensions between the two powers and the limits of Persian expansion.
events.name: Cambyses II sends ambassadors to Macrobia

events.enhanced_description: Circa 525 BCE, coins began to feature images on both sides, marking a significant development in numismatics and the evolution of currency. This innovation reflected the growing sophistication of trade and commerce in ancient societies.
events.name: Coins start to have an image on two sides

events.enhanced_description: In 523 BCE, Darius I ascended to the throne of the Achaemenid Empire, succeeding Bardiya, who was believed to be a usurper. Darius's reign marked the beginning of significant administrative reforms and expansion of the Persian Empire, solidifying its power in the region.
events.name: Darius I succeeds Bardiya as ruler of Persia

events.enhanced_description: In 523 BCE, Darius I faced a rebellion in Babylon as part of his efforts to consolidate power over the newly acquired territories of the Persian Empire. The rebellion was ultimately suppressed, reinforcing Darius's authority and control over Babylon.
events.name: The Babylonian rebellion against Persian rule is suppressed

events.enhanced_description: In 523 BCE, Dao ascended to the throne of the Zhou dynasty in China, marking a significant moment in the dynasty's history. However, his reign was short-lived as he died later that year, leading to a period of instability in the Zhou dynasty.
events.name: Dao becomes King of the Zhou dynasty of China but dies before the end of the year

events.enhanced_description: Around 523 BCE, Cleomenes I succeeded his father Anaxandridas as king of Sparta. His reign was marked by significant military campaigns and political maneuvering, including conflicts with neighboring city-states and internal Spartan politics.
events.name: Cleomenes I succeeds Anaxandridas as king of Sparta

events.enhanced_description: In approximately 520 BCE, Darius I issued a decree to resume construction on the Temple in Jerusalem, which had been halted. This action was part of his broader policy of supporting local traditions and religions in the provinces of his empire, fostering loyalty among his subjects.
events.name: Darius I decrees that work on Jerusalem resume

events.enhanced_description: Circa 520 BCE, the Kore statue, believed to be from Chios, was created and is now housed in the Acropolis Museum in Athens. This work exemplifies the artistry of the Archaic period in Greece, showcasing the intricate details and stylistic developments of the time.
events.name: Kore from Chios is made

events.enhanced_description: Circa 520 BCE, a notable sarcophagus was crafted in Cerveteri, Italy, and is now displayed at the National Etruscan Museum in Rome. This piece reflects the Etruscan culture's artistic achievements and burial practices during this period.
events.name: Sarcophagus from Cerveteri is made

events.enhanced_description: Darius I issued a decree for the resumption of work on Jerusalem, following the earlier edict of Cyrus the Great. This decision was pivotal for the Jewish community, facilitating the rebuilding of the Temple and the restoration of their religious practices.
events.name: Darius I decrees work on Jerusalem resumes

events.enhanced_description: In 519 BC, Cleomenes I, King of Sparta, advised the Plataeans to ally with Athens instead of Sparta, aiming to incite conflict between Thebes and Athens. This strategic maneuvering reflects the complex political landscape of ancient Greece.
events.name: Cleomenes advises Plataeans

events.enhanced_description: Around 518 BC, Darius I began the construction of Persepolis, which would become the ceremonial capital of the Persian Empire. This monumental project symbolized the power and cultural aspirations of Darius's reign.
events.name: Darius I begins constructing Persepolis

events.enhanced_description: The construction of the Apadana, the grand audience hall at Persepolis, began under Darius I and continued under Xerxes I around 518 BC. This architectural marvel served as a symbol of the grandeur of the Achaemenid Empire and its artistic achievements.
events.name: Construction of the Apadana at Persepolis

events.enhanced_description: Demaratus succeeded his father, Ariston, as King of Sparta, continuing the legacy of leadership in one of the most powerful city-states of ancient Greece. His reign would be marked by the ongoing tensions and conflicts with neighboring states.
events.name: Demaratus Succeeds Ariston as King of Sparta

events.enhanced_description: Zhou jing wang ascended to the throne of the Zhou Dynasty, a significant period in Chinese history marked by feudalism and the development of Chinese philosophy. His reign contributed to the consolidation of power and the cultural advancements of the dynasty.
events.name: Zhou Jing Wang becomes king of the Zhou dynasty
